conventions.convention: The slow update uses the initial pair, and every fast microstep uses the original frozen slow state. H>0 and the microstep count is a positive integer. Domain-exit returns no macro output.
Block errors use the product Euclidean norm. Field bounds and joint Lipschitz bounds hold on a common set containing the states being compared.
The global theorem assumes successful numerical runs and successful exact-start comparison runs with the same block-specific microstep counts, all within the common bounded Lipschitz set.
Waveform updates and integrals are exact mathematical operations. Admissibility requires MΔ≤R and q=KΔ<1. Sweep zero returns no certificate; positive sweeps use E_k=q^kδ_0/(1-q).
Symmetric interpolation means I_H(1−θ;v,u)=I_H(θ;u,v), and symmetric stepping means Ψ_−H=Ψ_H inverse where defined. Cubic defect and one-step stability are separate uniform premises.

load_bearing.statement: For admitted inputs, set h=H/m and x⁺=x+Hf(x,z), then perform z_{j+1}=z_j+h g(x,z_j), j=0,…,m−1, with x frozen. Check each evaluation state and the final output against the open domain; return success only when all required checks pass.
For the stated continuous field, exact solution and frozen microstates in a common set where ‖F‖₂≤M, ‖U(b)−U(a)‖₂≤M(b−a) for 0≤a≤b≤H, and ‖z_j−z_0‖₂≤jhM for 0≤j≤m.

For two successful runs with the same H,m, all compared inputs and microstates in a jointly K-Lipschitz set, and 0<H≤T, the output difference is at most (1+L_T H) times the input difference, where L_T=K√(2(1+exp(2KT))), independently of m.
Under the stated common-domain boundedness and joint Lipschitz assumptions for the exact path and exact-start microstates, the successful macro output satisfies ‖(x⁺,z_m)−U(H)‖₂≤4KMH².

On the admitted radius-R waveform set, iterate Φ(U)(t)=u_0+∫_0^t F(U(s)) ds synchronously from the constant waveform, subject to the finite sweep budget, and certify tolerance only when q^kδ_0/(1−q)≤ε.

published_dependencies.used_for: Continuous Euclidean-valued waveforms in the waveform algorithm.
Domain-relative derivatives, componentwise integrals, orientation, and integral additivity.
Exact solutions, including one-sided derivatives at time endpoints.
Exact-path integral identities and identification of the waveform fixed point with an IVP solution.
Product Euclidean norm and block-coordinate estimates.
Triangle inequalities, projection bounds, and the elementary Frobenius matrix bound.
Integral norm bounds on increasing intervals, including zero-length intervals.
Bounding integrals of nonnegative integrands by constant times interval length.
Exponential normalization in stability estimates and the linear example.
Natural powers in microstep amplification estimates, including exponent zero.
Raising nonnegative amplification-factor inequalities to integer powers.
Bounding microstep amplification and proving decay in the linear example.
Combining repeated exponential factors and expressing negative exponentials as reciprocals.
Uniform exponential bounds over H≤T.
Mean-value estimate of exponential increments and verification of exact linear solutions.
Exponential increment bound and nonincrease of the electromechanical energy.
Completeness of the ambient waveform space.
The choice-free closed-subspace direction establishing completeness of X_R.
Existence, uniqueness, convergence, and the finite-iterate tail bound for waveform iteration.
Componentwise integrability of continuous vector integrands.
Continuity of components and norms in the local-defect argument.
